gap: No result ChatGPT got states which power banks can run these projectors. XGIMI says the MoGo 4 and MoGo 4 Laser need a third-party USB-C PD bank or adapter that delivers 65–150 W, at 65 W/20 V/3.25 A or 100 W/20 V/5 A. BenQ's spec sheet lists the GV50's USB-C PD input as 20 V at 2.25–5 A (45–100 W). The Nebula Mars 3 Air takes power from a 19 V/4.74 A DC input and has no USB-C port. The GV50's one-cable USB-C video works only with the original Nintendo Switch: BenQ says a Switch 2 needs Nintendo's dock and HDMI.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited RTINGS pages (best portable, best under $1,000) and dupple.com's 2026 guide, which covers the MoGo 4, MoGo 4 Laser, Mars 3 Air and Mars 3. Dupple's only power-bank mention is that the JMGO PicoPlay 'runs from a power bank,' with no wattage, and it says nothing about Switch or HDR-over-HDMI limits. When fetched, the RTINGS pages showed only the title and navigation, not the article body, so I could not check their USB-C content. What Hi-Fi returned only its title, and aglena.com failed on an SSL error. ChatGPT's answer itself treats all five as interchangeable '2.5 hrs battery' models and gives no charging-input or console compatibility.
decides: For a shopper who wants to go past the 2.5-hour battery with a power bank, this splits the picks. The MoGo 4, MoGo 4 Laser and BenQ GV50 can run from a USB-C PD power bank, but the XGIMIs need a bank that holds at least 65 W at 20 V, so a typical 45 W bank is outside XGIMI's stated range. The Mars 3 Air cannot charge over USB-C at all. Within XGIMI, the MoGo 4 Laser accepts HDR10 over HDMI and the plain MoGo 4 does not. For Switch 2 owners, the GV50's selling point of one USB-C cable for video and power does not apply. Price check: on 2026-11-14 the MoGo 4 Laser alone was $669 at us.xgimi.com. The $749 ChatGPT showed matches XGIMI's MoGo 4 Laser Outdoor Collection bundle, not the projector alone.
